q: The paper's Fig 3e taxonomic-distribution claim uses 'homologues' without an explicit %-identity or coverage threshold. Different cutoffs would give very different distribution counts (e.g. GIY-YIG is universally distributed at the domain level but the *operonic* PD-T4-3 system may be much narrower). Does the 'broad' claim reflect true system spread or single-domain ancestry?
basis: Independent CD-Search shows GIY-YIG-family hits in essentially all bacterial phyla, but this reflects the ancient enzymatic domain, not the co-occurring operonic system. The paper's Fig 3e appears to conflate domain-level and system-level conservation.
next_steps: For each of the 21 systems, rerun BLASTP at graded %-identity thresholds (30, 50, 70%). Then additionally require operon-level co-occurrence — i.e., all components of a multi-gene system must be present within 10 kb on the same contig. Report a per-system 'true defence-system spread' metric distinct from single-domain spread.

q: For 6 of the 21 systems (PD-T4-5, PD-T4-7, PD-T4-9, PD-T4-10, PD-T7-1, PD-T7-3, PD-T7-5), NCBI CD-Search returns NO Pfam/COG hits and current NCBI annotations remain 'hypothetical'. This includes the paper's putative HEPN (PD-T7-3) and Abi (PD-T4-5) systems. Are these truly novel-fold proteins, or artifacts of the fosmid selection whose remote-homology signals aren't reliable?
basis: The paper's classification of these systems rests on HHpred remote homology + wet-lab EOP validation, both of which sit at the edge of what is currently detectable. If AlphaFold2 / ESMFold structural clustering places these into known folds, the novelty claim is weaker than presented.
next_steps: Predict structures for all 32 defence proteins with ESMFold or ColabFold. Cluster against AlphaFold DB + PDB via Foldseek. Classify per-system 'structural novelty' vs 'sequence novelty'. Report which of the 6 no-CDD-hit systems fall into known folds (e.g. HEPN, Abi coiled-coil, ATPase-nuclease fusions) and which are genuinely new.

q: The MGE/prophage-context claim replicated at 21/21 in our ±15 kb window — even stronger than the paper's qualitative Fig 4. This raises the reciprocal question: what is the *false discovery rate* of the tab selection? Of all prophage/ICE/transposon cargo genes on E. coli mobile elements, what fraction give a phage-defence phenotype when cloned into K-12?
basis: The paper's tab selection strongly enriched for prophage-neighborhood proteins (100% in our replication). Without a matched-negative-control experiment, we cannot know whether the selection is enriching real defence systems specifically, or prophage cargo genes generally (many prophage-encoded proteins have host-modulating effects unrelated to defence).
next_steps: From the same 71 strains, select a matched set of prophage/MGE cargo genes NOT called as defence systems in the screen. Clone them into the paper's vector, subject to identical tab selection, and measure EOP against T4/λvir/T7. Report FDR = fraction of matched non-hit prophage-cargo genes that also reduce EOP.

q: Table S4 uses %-identity to a single Gao 2020 seed sequence per component. Modern defence-detection pipelines (DefenseFinder 2.x, PADLOC 2026) use HMM profiles over whole system families, which are more sensitive. How many of the 18/32 'novel' components (no Gao hit) are recovered by DefenseFinder or PADLOC in 2026?
basis: DefenseFinder and PADLOC HMM libraries have expanded substantially since the 2022 paper (DefenseFinder v2 now covers >150 system families vs ~90 in 2022). If several PD systems now hit these HMMs, the 'novelty' claim is correct as of 2022 but the systems are already reclassified today.
next_steps: Run DefenseFinder 2.x and PADLOC 2026 against the 71-strain proteome (or at minimum against the 32 defence proteins). Report per-system 2022-novel-vs-2026-known status. This directly measures how quickly the anti-phage defence field is closing the gaps the paper opened.

q: Seven of the 21 systems sit in intact prophage neighborhoods with 5+ structural markers (capsid + tail + portal + terminase + integrase) in ±15 kb — PD-T4-6/7/8/9/10, PD-T7-3, PD-λ-5. Are these genuine bacterial defence systems captured by prophages (paper's implicit framing), or phage-encoded superinfection-exclusion modules that only *incidentally* protect the K-12 host against unrelated phages?
basis: Prophage-encoded superinfection-exclusion (Sie) systems are well documented (λ vs T4, P22 sieA/B, etc.). A prophage-cargo protein tested in tab selection cannot distinguish 'defence against T4 that happens to be located in a prophage' from 'prophage Sie module that happens to also block T4'. The 100% MGE-context result makes this ambiguity central to the paper's interpretation.
next_steps: For each of these 7 intact-prophage systems, test EOP against (a) the panel phage (paper's assay) and (b) the resident prophage itself, induced or in trans. If protection is selective for the panel phage and neutral toward the resident prophage → bona fide bacterial-defence acquisition. If protection extends to the resident prophage → superinfection-exclusion module, reclassify.
